dedupe_keys.name: global food system from photosynthesis to metabolism energetic closure at 1 degree resolution 1990 to 2019

description: This case study harmonises data on 95 food commodities across production, processing, animal feed and consumption into one energy framework, and links food supply to human metabolic demand estimated from body size, demographics and activity. The authors released the framework as open source and posted the work as a preprint, free to read online on arXiv. Coverage is global, on a 1-degree grid (about 10,000 square kilometres), from 1990 to 2019. Caveats: the preprint has not been peer reviewed, and metabolic demand and losses are modelled from national and gridded statistics. The study estimates that the share of food calories available for human consumption that is not metabolised doubled from about 10 percent to 20 percent between 1990 and 2019 as supply outpaced energy expenditure, and that about 51 percent of the world population's metabolic demand could in theory be met from production in the same grid cell with diets held constant. Simulation uses: a gridded baseline of food supply and demand for food supply network, localisation and shock models. Related records: the traceable food balance sheets (data-traceable-food-balance-sheets-gcamfaostat) and MapSPAM crop production (data-mapspam-spatial-production-allocation) are data of the kind the framework harmonises.
